Original calls slot 84 with edx=vtable pointer; reference passes nullptr, which is equivalent for a __thiscall callee. Return of the final call is taken as int. Helper name is my own; the anchor ratio logic follows the verified reference.

name: MenuMpPause_HandleMessage
summary: Handles a CMenuMpPause message: ids 1/14 forward a command to MenuMpPause_ProcessCommandId; id 50 with payload byte +0x38 set notifies the pause subsystem (vtable slot 7); every path ends by forwarding to ForwardUnhandledMenuMessage.
notes: GetMenuPauseSubsystem (0x6683F0) is a lib function with unknown prototype; it is modeled as __thiscall with no args returning a pointer, based on ecx=this with no pushes. The subsystem's vtable slot 7 call is unnamed. Names for 0x534AE0 and 0x428480 are inferred from usage.

name: CMenuIntroVideo_Tick
summary: Per-frame update of the intro video: notifies global state (vtable slot 23, code 11), then either begins playback when the global gate opens (phase 0) or advances the timer and finishes (phase 1).
notes: CMenuIntroVideo_BeginPlayback (0x535900) and IsGlobalIntGateOpen (0x6B1680) are unnamed; names are guesses from usage. Return of 0x6B1680 is read as a byte (al). Vtable slot 0x5C used on the global state object is assumed to be a notify/event method; the object's type is unknown, so it is accessed via CSF_AT(void**, ...).

name: CMenuGameOptions_InitializeAndRefresh
summary: Initializes the game options menu: stores a2 in field_0018, applies global value state, runs a sequence of virtual refresh calls, and returns field_001c.
notes: Callee sub_521DE0 is bound as taking one thiscall-style pointer arg (ecx only) and is treated as void-returning. Vtable slot 0x16c on the object at field_001c and slot 0x44 call results are ignored. Slot-by-slot semantics are inferred from the disassembly; the names of the virtual methods are unknown. The 0x1c object's type is unknown, so its vtable is accessed via CSF_AT. Hook pops 8 bytes as the original does.

name: CMenuSaveGame_ResolvePanelAndApplyScale
summary: Caches the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL element in self+0x44 on first call, then scales it by the anchor position relative to screen width/height via the panel's vtable slot 84.
notes: Hex-Rays pseudocode shows bogus register-propagated args on the calls to 0x652160 and the slot-6 call; the disassembly has no pushed args there, so those calls take only ecx. a5 is dereferenced into ecx and used as this for 0x693360, so it is a live read. Ratios are computed in double then cast to float, as in the verified 0x52BD10 clone; the original computes in x87 80-bit, so a last-bit difference is possible.

name: CMenuMpGameMode_ResolvePanelAndApplyScale
summary: Caches the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL element from the screen's root object in field_0018 and, on first success, calls the panel's vtable slot 84 with X/Y ratios computed from two looked-up anchors divided by screen width/height.
notes: Same shape as 0x0052BD10. Stack args are (screen, registryHolder), ret 8 matches. Callee 0x652160 is bound with the same fastcall signature as the reference. The x87 extended-precision division is approximated with double then float, as in the verified reference. Vtable slot 84 callee pops its own float args (assumed, as in the reference).

name: CMenuProgressBar_ResolvePanelAndApplyRatio
summary: Caches the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL panel in field_0020 on first call, then passes X/Y anchor ratios (anchor divided by screen width/height) to the panel's vtable slot 84.
notes: Stack args: screen (ebp+8, vtable slot 21 yields root object) and registryHolder (ebp+0xc, dereferenced for the registry). Return value of the final virtual call is passed through as eax. Conversions use double where the original uses x87 extended precision; the same approach as the verified 0x52BD10 clone. The stored [ebp+8] writes in the original overwrite the screen argument slot, which is not read afterward, so they are not reproduced. Callee 0x652160 is treated as __fastcall(int, void*) as in the verified clone.

name: MenuMpOnline_ResetSession
summary: Resets the online MP session: conditionally resets global state if flag F0 is set, calls two virtual methods (sub-object at +0x3C slot 25, self slot 21), clears g_MpSessionState, then calls sub_50F790 with tag 0x494C3237 and returns its result.
notes: Self class id unknown, so self is void* and offsets use CSF_AT. Field at +0x3C is treated as an object pointer (loaded with mov ecx,[esi+0x3c]). sub_50E1E0 and sub_50F790 are bound by address with guessed names; their semantics are unknown. Object_IsFieldF0NonZero result is tested via the low byte (al) to match 'test al, al'.

name: CMenuProfiles_ResolvePanelAndApplyScale
summary: Lazily resolves the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL panel from the screen's root object, caches it in +0x24, then scales it by the anchor-to-screen ratios (X and Y) via vtable slot 84; returns the cached panel if already set.
notes: Clone of 0x0052BD10 with the cached field at +0x24 (accessed via CSF_AT since it is not a declared field) and stack args (screen, registryHolder) with ret 8. Callee ABI for the slot-84 call is assumed to match the reference (__fastcall with nullptr edx, two float stack args, callee-cleaned); the disassembly shows no caller cleanup after it. Double-precision ratio math follows the verified reference rather than the x87 80-bit intermediate.

name: CMenuOptions_ResolvePanelAndApplyScale
summary: Lazily resolves and caches the '.PANEL_PRINCIPAL' panel in field_001c, then scales it by the anchor-to-screen ratios via the panel's vtable slot 84.
notes: Hex-Rays lists ebx/esi as inputs and passes them to the slot-0x18 call, but the disassembly shows no argument pushes there; the slot-0x18 calls take no args and the anchor X/Y are read from offsets 0 and 4 of the results, so the disassembly was followed. The vtable call at slot 84 is treated as taking two float args (X/width first, Y/height second) and returning int, with its callee popping 8 bytes; the return value is passed through as the function result. Callee 0x652160 is bound as a fastcall taking one int in ecx, matching the reference. Calling convention of 0x693360 assumed thiscall with one stack arg.

name: CMenuCredits_DestroyAndMaybeFree
summary: CMenuCredits destructor: resets vtables, releases the child at +0x18 via slot-0 deleting call, destroys the embedded member at +0x20, restores CMenuScreen vtable, and frees the object if the flag's low bit is set. Returns this.
notes: Child at +0x18 is called with slot 0 and arg 1 (deleting-destructor convention), then the field is zeroed. The +0x4 field is written as a raw vtable pointer and is the CMenuScreen base slot. The embedded object at +0x20 is passed by address (lea). The object type of +0x18 is unknown, so it is handled through void** and CSF_AT. The ret 4 pop matches the single char argument.

name: CMenuMpSessions_ProcessSessionTransition
summary: Processes multiplayer session transitions, updates menu flags, and dispatches the appropriate menu event.
notes: The meaning of 0x734A10 is inferred; it is called with this and no stack arguments. The no-op at 0x506AC0 receives the explicit cdecl argument shown in assembly. The return preserves the original EAX value.

name: CMenuAccountEdit_DestroyAndMaybeFree
summary: Destructor body for CMenuAccountEdit: releases the child at +0x284 via its slot-0 deleting destructor, tears down the embedded member at +0x34, restores the CMenuScreen vtables, and frees the object if flag bit 0 is set; returns this.
notes: Original ret 4 and __thiscall convention match the signature. The 0x518890 callee is named by its embedded offset because its role is unknown. Vtable immediates 0x845438, 0x8453E8, 0x830488, 0x830438 are written as raw constants as in the reference shape. The +0x284 child is assumed to be an object with a deleting destructor at vtable slot 0, based on the call pattern.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_LoadObjectiveFromMissionData
summary: Returns 0 if the mission's objective entry list is empty (or has no full 80-byte entries); otherwise fetches a value via vtable slot 9 of the mission data object, passes it to the subpanel at this+0x30, and returns 1.
notes: Callee names are guesses: sub_515CE0 returns a list header {unk, begin, end} (GetObjectiveEntryList); sub_5150F0 takes this+0x30 and an int (ObjectivePanel_Assign). The division by 80 is signed (imul magic 0x66666667 plus sign fixup), reproduced with int32 arithmetic. The original's [ebp-4] spill is dead and omitted. Return is a byte (xor al,al / mov al,1), so char is used.

name: CMenuAccounts_ProcessSchedulerProxyState
summary: Runs a no-op, then dispatches on the state field at +0x28: state 1 and 2 forward to helpers, states 3/4 fetch the scheduler proxy and, if present, call a virtual slot and mark state as 1; state 0 and others return the state value.
notes: Helper 0x5650F0 is unnamed (semantics unknown); 0x734A10 is treated as a __thiscall with no stack args (rets=0). Return value is the int in eax. Vtable slot 24 (offset 0x60) is the virtual call on the state-3/4 path. Confirm the vtable-slot convention for CSF_AT(void**, self, 0)[24] against the gate.

name: CMenuMpOnline_InitMainPanelAndFriendsButton
summary: Lazily resolves the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL panel, positions it from layout records scaled by screen size, then fetches the BotonFriends button, stores it, and calls its slot 42 with 1.
notes: The Hex-Rays pseudocode passes the saved ebx/edi as two stack args to the record slot-6 call, but the asm pushes nothing there, so the call is emitted with no args and the entry pushes are left for the epilogue, matching the asm. Slot 42 (+0xA8) on the button is assumed to return int; its return value is returned directly. The FindUiElementByName/ResolveObjectFromIntId calling conventions are inferred from the same-shape reference and not independently verified.

name: MenuMpAccounts_OnStateTransition
summary: Queries the global state object; if the query returns nonzero and not 2, returns that value; if it returns 2, invokes a vtable method and sets state field +0x280 to 9; if it returns 0, resets a slot, submits request 0x41453231, sets state +0x280 to 3, and returns the submit result.
notes: Owning class unknown, so the field at +0x280 is accessed via CSF_AT. Two distinct GetGlobalState addresses (0x50D190, 0x6A6D70) are bound as GetGlobalStateObjectA and GetGlobalStateObjectB; the names are placeholders chosen for distinctness. Helper names ResetGlobalStateSlot and SubmitGlobalStateRequest are inferred from usage only. Vtable slots 7 (0x1c) and 17 (0x44) are unidentified. The 0x6A6D70 object's vtable call at slot 17 has an unknown return meaning, but its return value is passed through to the caller as in the original.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_RefreshAllFiveFlag
summary: Conditionally recomputes and caches the all-entries-are-five flag for a panel object when the tab index is in range, the game state is ready, and the global default entry has no pending value at +0x1C.
notes: Return value is reproduced through al: early exits return the low byte of the value that was last in eax (tabIndex, the flag byte, or the entry pointer), matching the disassembly. The name of 0x4FE4A0 and the return type of 0x44FB00 are inferred from usage. Callee 0x53E1C0 is stdcall per the packet, although the caller also sets ecx=this, which a stdcall callee ignores. The second entry lookup dereferences its result without a null check, as the original does.

name: MenuCharSelect_TickPreviewLoop
summary: Runs the MP character-select camera preview wait loop while the global state reports phase 7 (stepping phase 3 with a 0.01s timer), then finalizes the preview slot from the global dword.
notes: Disassembly shows the first GetGlobalState/vtable slot 0x1C check, then a loop with GetGlobalDword_73C020 called twice (once discarded, once as this for the timer call); preserved as-is. Slot 0x18 takes a float on the stack (callee pops 4), modeled as __fastcall with a float arg. Tail jmp to sub_73E920 (__thiscall, no stack args, ret 0) is reproduced as a normal call returning its eax, which is equivalent for a no-arg cdecl caller. Global-state class and phase semantics are unknown; vtable accessed via CSF_AT since the type is not declared.

name: CMenuPlayerList_BuildPlayerStatusIcons
summary: Builds account and connection icon text and returns combined player-status flags.
notes: Formatter arguments use a trivial 28-byte by-value string representation. The precise meaning of the alternate player-state predicate is unknown.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_EnterPanelState
summary: Resets bichos photo flags, notifies owner at +0x10 and global state, calls virtual on panel at +0x1c and releases child at +0x84 (returns its result).
notes: Gate fix: 0x53D530 pops 0 bytes and has no stack args, so it is declared __fastcall(self, edx) which also pops 0. Limitation: the original 0x53D530 is __usercall and reads edi (a2) on entry; this wrapper cannot forward edi, so that callee may see a stale edi. Preserving edi would need a naked thunk, which was not used here. Also the sub_50DC80 return value is unused and declared void, and CSF_AT(uint8_t, ...) is assumed to yield an lvalue byte.

name: CMenuPause_CloseAndReturnResult
summary: Toggles the menu child flag, optionally sets a global-state aux flag, notifies the global state's child object (vtbl+0x24) and this menu's child (vtbl+0x60 with self,1), then finalizes and returns a result via sub_42DF80.
notes: Role of the callees (sub_50DC80 sets a flag on the global state; sub_42DF80 finalizes/consumes a result) is inferred. sub_42DF80 receives the GetGlobal8afc78 result in ecx and a2 on the stack; it is bound as __fastcall with an explicit ecx parameter to match the disassembly, since the Hex-Rays prototype shows only a stdcall stack arg (both pop 4). The return value of sub_50DC80 (bool) is unused and ignored. The GetGlobalState call count (3 or 4) follows the original exactly.

name: CMenuEula_LoadTextIntoNameAndSetState
summary: Fetches a text string from the provider object at +0x34 via vtable slot 0x93, assigns it into the member string at +0x3C, sets +0x18 to 2, and frees the temporary string's heap buffer if capacity >= 8.
notes: Temporary std::string layout inferred from the MSVC 7.1 layout (buffer at +0x04, size at +0x14, capacity at +0x18 within the frame); the sret slot address (ebp-0x1C) sits 4 bytes before the buffer, so the frame is modeled as a raw byte array to match the original offsets exactly. Return type of 0x488830 is treated as void*. Vtable slot 0x93 signature (sret pointer, int) is inferred from the push order. The return of the free path is the Mem_FreeDebug result, as in the original.

name: MenuMissionInfo_AssignFromArray
summary: Assigns an 8-byte-element array (data, capacity, count, extra) from a source object, reallocating the buffer via the game heap when the source count exceeds capacity, then copying elements and the count/extra fields; returns this.
notes: Class id unknown, so fields use CSF_AT offsets (0x00 data ptr, 0x04 capacity, 0x08 count, 0x0C extra). The inline rep movsd is reproduced as a dword loop without calling any function. Count compare is unsigned (jbe). Return is full eax (this), declared void*.

name: CMenuVideoOptions_ApplySelection
summary: Stores a selection index, resyncs the quality preset and global value, and conditionally rebuilds the options menu; returns a byte.
notes: The original pushes selectionIndex before calling 0x521BB0 and leaves it on the stack for 0x5231D0 (ret 4). The packet gives 0x521BB0 as zero-arg cdecl, so the pushed value is not modeled in the call; this is stack-neutral only if 0x521BB0 does not read its stack args. Preset-change vtable slot 170 (0x2A8) signature is assumed (void __fastcall, int). 0x734A10 is assumed to be a thiscall with no stack args returning int. Return type is char because the paths return a bare low byte of eax.

name: MenuMpOnline_HandleConnectionState
summary: Checks a global state object's virtual state value; if nonzero, handles state 2 by resetting the online session and setting this+0x18 to 4, otherwise resets the session, runs a virtual method on this, and shows dialog 0x4C413331.
notes: Two different callees are both named GetGlobalState in the packet; 0x6A6D70 is bound as GetActiveStateManager (its object's vtable slot 7 returns an int). Function names for 0x50E1E0 (ResetOnlineSession) and 0x50F790 (ShowDialogById) are guesses from behaviour. The this+0x18 field is accessed via CSF_AT since the class layout is not declared here. The dialog ID 0x4C413331 is treated as an opaque constant.

name: MenuSaveGame_RefreshLayoutForScheduler
summary: Checks the scheduler proxy kind (4 or 8); for 4 it calls a virtual on a child entry, then resets the menu state, calls a layout virtual, clears the stats sub-object and forwards to the layout routine.
notes: The original is __usercall with ebx as an input, and that value is passed to 0x541570 in ebx. Pure C++ cannot set ebx on the call, so this file passes it only as a stack argument omitted from the call; the call to 0x541570 is therefore incomplete and the forwarded ebx is lost. The function parameter carries ebx through edx, which assumes the hook adapter maps ebx to edx; this needs verification. sub_541650 and 0x734A10 were given placeholder-free names but their true class names are unknown. Field types are uint32_t/int via CSF_AT because no declared struct fields were given for this class.

name: MenuManager_TransitionToGameOrIntro
summary: Transitions menu pages into gameplay or an intro flow and updates associated state.
notes: Assembly establishes one unused stack argument and no incoming EBX/EDI/ESI arguments. The intro setter receives the embedded descriptor, not a page-name string. The 0x42DF80 binding supplies ECX as shown by the caller while retaining its four-byte stack cleanup; its precise semantics remain uncertain.

name: CMenuDemoExit_Activate
summary: Activates the demo-exit screen: stores the manager, resets the timer, refreshes global value and GUI, optionally shows the demo-exit notice, and returns the GUI pointer.
notes: Semantics of sub_521DE0 (GlobalValue_Refresh) and sub_50E1E0 (GlobalState_ShowDemoExitNotice) are guessed from call context only. Vtable slot 0x16c on m_pGui is called with no arguments; its meaning is unknown. The a3 argument is popped but unused, matching ret 8.

name: CMenuPause_OnContinueClicked
summary: Continue button handler: if the pause field is set, refreshes two global-value subsystems, notifies the owner object's virtual method with g_pszMenu_P_Juego (and optionally a result target), then closes the screen with code 0; otherwise returns the zero field.
notes: Callee sub_521F80 and sub_5233D0 are unnamed; they were given provisional names (ProcessGlobalValueHandle, ApplyGlobalValueToSubsystem) based on how they receive GetGlobalValue's result. Return value of sub_539D10 is treated as a close code call with argument 0. Owner and notify-target vtable slots (0x5C, 0x54) are inferred from the disassembly and their meanings are unknown.

name: CMenuMpServerInfo_DecrementRotationTimer
summary: Decrements the float timer at +0x4C by a float argument unless the byte at +0x1F4 is set, sets a negative flag via SetRotationWrapFlag, and wraps the timer by adding a constant when it goes below zero.
notes: The wrap constant at 0x82E1E4 is taken as 3.0 from the Hex-Rays pseudocode; its real float value is not verified. GetGlobalValue is declared with one ignored cdecl argument because the original pushes a2 before calling it and that value is later popped by 0x5231D0. The name ApplyGlobalValueDelta for 0x5231D0 and SetRotationWrapFlag for 0x5322A0 are guesses from usage. The flag is computed as (value < 0.0) per the x87 fcomp/test ah,5 sequence.

name: CMenuMpOnline_ActivateOnlineMenu
summary: Notifies the child menu at +0x3C, queries it with the g_pszMenu_P_Juego handle, and if not handled, refreshes network mode flags and tail-calls session setup.
notes: Assumed __cdecl for 0x6A6D40 (void, no args), and 0x73E920 treated as __thiscall with ret 0 (tail-jumped). Object at +0x3C is typed void* via CSF_AT since its class is not declared. Vtable slot calls 24/23/29 taken from offsets 0x60/0x5C/0x74. Return of the vtable slot-29 call is kept as full int, since the caller tests the low byte and returns eax unchanged.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_ClosePanelAndDeactivate
summary: If the panel is active and the global scheduler proxy equals 16, prepares the panel, resets the child object's state, then either invokes the virtual slot 0x48 on self or resets panels, and clears the active flag.
notes: Fixed the compile errors by using the declared type CMenuMissionInfo instead of C_CMenuMissionInfo. The original is __usercall and reads edi (a2) and forwards it to sub_53D740; edi is not forwarded here, since C++ cannot express it without inline asm, so the hook may not be exact. The callee's name and argument semantics, and the meaning of field_0014, are guesses. The vtable slot for field_001c's object type is unknown, so CSF_AT is used.

name: CMenuEula_ReleaseResources
summary: Tears down CMenuEula state: releases the helper object via its vtable slot 0, frees the primary and secondary buffers, resets size/flags, and restores the CMenuScreen base vtables.
notes: Return value follows Hex-Rays (last free result or 0); eax at the original's exit is path-dependent and the caller likely ignores it. Vtable addresses 0x841B78/0x841BC8 and 0x830488/0x830438 are written as immediates; C_ class id prefix assumed to be CMenuEula. Field 0x40 is cleared as a 16-bit store, matching the original.

name: MenuSaveGame_ResetState
summary: Resets a CMenuSaveGame: zeroes slot-range pointers/count, reinitializes the sub-object at +0x14 with the global flag byte, clears +0x30, frees the slot buffer via ClearSlotRange and Mem_FreeDebug if present, and returns this.
notes: ClearSlotRange is called with 4 cdecl args per the disassembly (first, last, this+4, this); the Hex-Rays 2-arg prototype was incomplete. The word store at +0x18 and dword stores at +0x28/+0x2C are inferred from the ecx=this+0x14 offsets. The write of 0 to [this] happens before the sub-object call, matching the original order. The callee sub_697130 is treated as a thiscall returning a pointer whose result is unused.

name: CMenuMpOnline_UpdateAndDispatch
summary: Updates shared managers and dispatches the online menu's current state unless menu processing is blocked.
notes: The two global-state getters are distinct. State 18 forwards the argument's raw bits as a float; opaque helper names are descriptive guesses.

name: CMenuSaveGame_Construct
summary: CMenuSaveGame constructor: installs vtables 0x83042C, 0x843B70 (sub-object) and 0x843B30, constructs base and embedded sub-objects, stores ownerContext at +0x48, zeroes list state, sets two fields to -1 and stores a dword from a global record at +0x58; returns this.
notes: The gate reported vtable references 0x83042C, 0x843B30 and 0x843B70 as missing. The previous file declared them via CSF_GLOBAL but stored only through named references; this version writes the exact literal vtable addresses in the stores while keeping the CSF_GLOBAL bindings. Embedded sub-objects at +0x04 and +0x5C are constructed via 0x712CC0 and 0x5445F0; their semantics are unverified. Field names for +0x50/+0x54 (-1 defaults) are guesses. Callee pops 4 (ret 4).

name: CMenuSaveGame_SetProgressAndDispatchMode
summary: Stores the float stack argument at +0x4C, applies it to the global value, then dispatches on the mode at +0x50 (0/1/5 special cases) and refreshes the buttons.
notes: ApplyStoredValueToGlobal (0x5231D0) is a __thiscall with one stack arg (ret 4), now bound as __fastcall(self, edx, value) to match the gate. The original passes a2 (ebx) and a3 (edi) as usercall register args to sub_544B90, sub_544A50 and sub_5458D0. Those registers cannot be set from C++ without inline asm, so the calls here pass only ecx/edx; the callees may read stale ebx/edi. The return of sub_5458D0 is discarded, as in the original. The callee names are guesses based on their call sites.

name: CMenuMessageBox_RefreshLayoutAndButtons
summary: Fetches a child object from the sub-object at +0x894, builds a rect from the box's origin and extent and passes it to that sub-object, sets the child's overlay color, resets state fields, calls sub_52B020, updates the +0x894 object's flags and returns the result of its final vtable call; returns 0 when the child is null.
notes: Hex-Rays lists a2 (ebx) as an input, but the asm only saves and restores ebx, so the function takes just ecx. The vtable targets at +0x24/+0x1C on the child are treated as output getters for extent and origin, based on how the rect is built. g_fDimOverlayAlpha at 0x8413BC is assumed to be 127.0 and is read from memory as a float. sub_52B020's name is a guess and its return value's upper 24 bits are forwarded to +0x25C, replicating the sete-al behavior. Field 0x994 is not declared, so it is accessed with CSF_AT. The type of the +0x894 object and the semantics of its slots (0x16C, 0x1CC, 0x1DC, 0x208, 0x25C, 0xC0) are unknown. The meaning of the +0x2C target on the 0x1DC result is also unknown.

name: CMenuLoading_ReleaseMembersAndResetVtable
summary: Destructor body for CMenuLoading: releases owned sub-objects at +0x2C/+0x40/+0x4C/+0x54 (virtual slot 0 with flag 1), frees the block at +0x3C, tears down the embedded base at +0x10, and restores the vtables.
notes: Vtable stores are now written as literal addresses via CSF_AT at offsets 0x00, 0x04, 0x10, matching the original's store order (0x842150, 0x842100, 0x8420F8, then 0x830488, 0x830438, 0x83042C). The +0x2C object is read before the vtable stores, as the original reads it first. Return type of sub_6923C0 is treated as void since its result is unused.

name: MenuSystem_InitCommonMenuBuilder
summary: Loads Menus/P_Common.fbs into a target object, builds a 0xA8-byte menu object from two global lookups, stores it at self+0x14, assigns it to the panel at self+0x10, and copies self+0x10 into target+0x80.
notes: Callee 0x652160 has no known prototype; treated as __fastcall taking the index in ecx with no stack args (asm passes it in ecx and pops nothing). Callee 0x712E80 name and role are guesses. Self's class is unknown, so all fields use CSF_AT offsets. The virtual call at slot 0x94 is reconstructed from the Hex-Rays view; its result is used as the target object, as the disassembly shows.

name: CMenuOptions_SetupScreen
summary: Resets CMenuOptions state fields, stores the screen argument, looks up the BotonVideo/BotonSonido/BotonJuego child controls on the child screen object at +0x1C, lays them out, and returns the child object pointer.
notes: Slot 0x40 on self is assumed to be a no-arg virtual hook (void return). The 0x44 slot takes the child object as its single argument. The unused second stack argument (a3) is kept for the 8-byte ret. Names of sub_521DE0 (GlobalValue_Apply) and sub_53AD90 (CMenuOptions_LayoutOptionButtons) are guesses based on the calling context.

name: CMenuPause_CleanupAndEnterScreen
summary: Runs three global-state cleanup/reset calls, then enters the menu screen via CMenuScreen_Enter(this, 0) and returns its result.
notes: Callee names for 0x521F80, 0x5233D0, 0x501E50 and 0x539D10 are guesses based on context; 0x521F80 and 0x501E50 are bound with a fastcall ecx arg to match the disassembly, and their real convention is unverified. The return value of 0x501E50 is discarded, as in the original.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_UpdateAndForward
summary: If the panel is active and its sub-panel at this+0x30 is ready, resets and resyncs the panel with mission state, then forwards the event (a3) to the base handler.
notes: The original receives a2 in edi (__userpurge) and passes it to sub_53DC60 unchanged. Plain C++ cannot express reading or forwarding edi, so a2 is dropped here and sub_53DC60 is bound as __fastcall(self, edx, a3); this is not an exact ABI match and will need a naked thunk or inline-asm fix to preserve edi. ret 4 matches the original. Names for sub_5406A0, sub_53E040, sub_540700, and sub_53DC60 are guesses from their call sites. The class id and layout of CMenuMissionInfo are unknown, so self is void* and offset 0x30 is accessed by raw address arithmetic.

name: CMenuTextInput_Construct
summary: Constructs a CMenuTextInput: sets vtables (0x83042C base, then 0x841450 final, secondary 0x841400 at +0x04), initializes the CMenuScreen base at +0x04 and a sub-object at +0x34, stores the stack argument at +0x18, and zeroes state fields.
notes: Vtable addresses are now written as literal immediates matching the original's mov instructions, and the CSF_GLOBAL bindings are still referenced. The stack argument name and meaning are unknown. Sub-object at +0x34 fields (+0x38, +0x48, +0x4C) are accessed via CSF_AT because they are not declared. Callee 0x697130 is treated as __thiscall with ret 4 (ecx = this+0x34). Callee 0x712CC0 is treated as __thiscall with no args.

name: MenuProfiles_UpdateTrucoFlag
summary: Compares the truco string against the profile entry text; sets a flag byte on self (+0x40), a player-state byte (+0x50) and a session byte (+0xD2), returning the session global.
notes: Hex-Rays control flow is inverted in the else-branch; the disassembly was followed (je at 0x53c0d4 returns when the flag byte is zero). The return value keeps the compare result's upper eax bytes on the early-exit path. GetTrucoString is cdecl with no real args; the pushes before its call belong to CopyTrucoStringToWide. Callee names for 0x506BD0, 0x756A10, 0x75FDF0 are descriptive guesses, and their return types are assumed int.

name: MenuMpCharacterSelect_RefreshCameraPreview
summary: If the global state flag at +208 is set, resolves the MP spawn index from the global int, applies it, refreshes the preview camera of the owner object (this->owner+24), then clears this+0xA and sets this+0xC to -1.0f.
notes: Callee sub_5500F0 and sub_555DD0 are declared bool in the packet but their results are discarded; bound as int with the same arg counts, which does not change behavior. The this-object class is unknown, so offsets use CSF_AT. Return is the GetGlobalState pointer unless the branch overwrites it with sub_555DD0's result. Not compiled or verified.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_InitializeMainPanel
summary: Lazily resolves and scales the main panel, finds exit controls, and creates its interface child.
notes: Assembly confirms two stack arguments with ret 8; EBX/EDI and the reported ST0 argument are decompiler artifacts.

name: MenuMain_ConsumePendingSelection
summary: Reads pending selection at +0x44, checks it against the global subobject; on match clears +0x44 to -1 and sets +0x14 to 2, then forwards the stack arg to the global dispatcher at 0x4FCEB0 and returns its al.
notes: The original passes the caller's edi unchanged as a2 to 0x4FCEB0 (userpurge). This C++ version cannot express reading/forwarding edi without inline asm, so the edi value reaching 0x4FCEB0 is whatever the compiler leaves in edi; a naked thunk would be needed for exact equivalence. Class id is unknown, so the self pointer is untyped. Return is the callee's al (char), no zeroing needed.

name: CMenuMpNetworkType_InitializeScreen
summary: Initializes the LAN/WAN network-type menu screen: resets its state, binds the BotonLAN, BotonWAN and StaticInfo controls from the GUI object, refreshes global menu state, resets the account selection, scrolls the viewport and returns the GUI object pointer.
notes: The original-name collision: 0x50D190 and 0x6A6D70 are both 'GetGlobalState' in the packet; they are renamed GetGlobalStateRoot and GetGlobalStateObject here. 0x521DE0 (ApplyGlobalValueBinding) and 0x652160 (GetObjectForGlobalInt) have no known semantics; names are guesses, and 0x652160 is assumed to take its argument in ecx with no stack args (rets=0). The StaticInfo result is stored at +0x2C per the disassembly (the pseudocode line '+44' is the same offset). The third stack argument (a3 at [ebp+0xC]) is never read; it is kept only so the ret 8 matches. The entryArgument/field_0034 name is a guess based on the store from [ebp+8].

name: CMenuMessageBox_TryAttachResolvedEntry
summary: Resolves an entry from two args, tests it against a flag byte, and if it passes attaches it to the sub-object at +0x90 and sets the byte at +0x80 to 1.
notes: Return value is the full eax left by the last call (695680 returns __int16 but is declared int to preserve full eax); the early-return paths return 0 or the 695500 result, which is 0 when reached. Callee names are generic because their semantics are not yet known. Global 0x82E65C is passed by address as a byte flag; CSF_GLOBAL usage assumes it yields an lvalue. Class id for self is a guess.

name: CMenuGameOptions_SendOkQuestionGE03
summary: Looks up the BotonOkQuestion child, stores it at +0x28, and if the global flag at +0xCC is clear, sends the "GE03" message string through the child's vtable (slot 16) using a temporary std::string-like buffer, freeing its heap storage afterwards.
notes: The call to 0x692720 is cdecl with (&scratch, "GE03", 1); its real role is unclear, and the temporary buffer is never written by the function in the visible code, so the message text may be empty at runtime. The 0x8427FC reference is treated as a CSF_STR literal even though the packet lists it as data. GetGlobalValue's calling convention is assumed to be __cdecl with no arguments. The vtable slot 16 call's return value is kept as the function result. Field 0x28 is written as declared (the Hex-Rays +40 offset is the same byte as the asm +0x28).

name: CMenuProfilesPC_DispatchStateEvent
summary: Calls the CMenuProfiles base event handler with the event argument, then dispatches on the state word at +0x38 (cases 0, 2, 4, 5) and returns the handler result, or the raw state value for other states.
notes: The packet's Hex-Rays pseudocode maps case 4 to CMenuSaveGame_ResetSelection (0x5442E0) and case 5 to CMenuSaveGame_ShutdownAndReturnResult (0x5442A0). The disassembly blocks say the opposite: the block at 0x544716 (case 4 by address order) calls 0x5442A0 and the block at 0x544722 calls 0x5442E0. I followed the disassembly, since it is authoritative. The jump table at 0x544730 was not provided, so the case-to-block mapping is inferred from block order; cases 1 and 3 are assumed to go to default. The self parameter is typed void* because the CMenuProfilesPC struct name is not confirmed in auto_classes.h. The callee names for 0x5442A0 and 0x5442E0 come from the packet. Confirm the jump table before relying on the case 4/5 mapping.

name: CMenuScenarioSelect_Construct
summary: Constructs the scenario-selection menu, initializes embedded storage, and resets selection state.
notes: Vtable stores now explicitly contain the original addresses. Embedded constructor and storage calls now receive subobject addresses rather than loaded pointers. The reset call passes zero for its presumed unused EDX parameter; storage initialization semantics remain unverified.

name: CMenuPause_OpenSubmenuRequest
summary: Sets CMenuPause field +0x14 to 1, builds a 180-byte request buffer via 0x501870, tags it, dispatches it through the global state with code 0x67653130, then destroys the buffer and returns the destructor's result.
notes: Fixed the gate error: 0x501870 is __fastcall with only register args (ecx, edx) and pops 0 bytes, so the stack-arg parameter was removed. The caller's edx is forwarded unchanged, as the original never writes edx before that call. The 0x67653130 code is passed as a literal integer, not a string. The 0x501870 and 0x4FF3C0 roles are inferred from usage. edx values reaching later calls are passed as nullptr because the original's edx is clobbered by the intervening calls and the callees ignore it.

name: CMenuVideoAdvanced_InitializeAndLoadSettings
summary: Zeroes the advanced video option fields, stores the first argument at +0x14, runs the virtual init chain on self and the settings object at +0x1C, refreshes state and widgets, and returns the object at +0x1C.
notes: Hex-Rays shows the settings object via +0x1C in asm but +0x1C is read via [esi+0x1c]; the pseudocode shows +0x1C as this+28 in one place, which is consistent. Callees 0x521DE0, 0x53AD90, 0x548D20 are treated as __thiscall with no stack args (ret 0). The virtual slot 0x44 call pushes the settings object as one argument. The hooked function's a3 is unused. Assumes CMenuVideoAdvanced is the declared struct name in types/auto_classes.h.

name: FormatCountText
summary: Formats the object's two counters at +0x2C/+0x30 into "{d0}/{d1}" text and assigns the result to the output string, returning it.
notes: Fixed the compile errors: CSF_STR is a two-argument expression macro, so it is now used inline at the call site instead of as a file-scope statement, and the nonexistent CSF_STR_PTR was removed. Stack-frame emulation is still approximate: the original passes its frame to the cdecl formatter 0x696A80 and cleans it with add esp,0x2C, which a C++ call cannot reproduce exactly; the frame struct only mirrors the memory order. Return type of 0x488830 and the string type were written as void* because std::_String_base is not confirmed in the allowed headers. The owning class of a1 is unknown, so its fields are accessed by offset.

name: CMenuControls_StepStateMachine
summary: Advances CMenuControls' pending-state machine (field_02dc): 0->1, 2->apply configuration rows and listbox add, 4->query scheduler proxy and refresh selection or reset state to -1; other values return state-4.
notes: 0x542EB0 is not a function start, so the tail-jump target is no longer bound; its body is reproduced inline in CMenuControls_ApplySelectedConfiguration (a file-local helper, not bound to 0x542EB0). Limitation: 0x42AF90 is usercall with esi=this and ebx=caller's ebx; this C++ wrapper cannot set esi or ebx, so it is bound as __cdecl with the three stack args only, and the callee's esi/ebx inputs are not reproduced. This may be wrong at runtime. Return of the apply path is eax from 0x716A60, bound as int-returning. 0x734A10 prototype is unknown and bound as __fastcall(this) returning int.

name: MenuMain_ClearPendingIndexAndForward
summary: Reads the pending index at +0x44, if a global sub-object's predicate matches it clears +0x14/+0x44 to -1 and calls the virtual reset slot (+0x58), then forwards the stack arg to the global handler at 0x4FCEB0.
notes: The original passes a2 in edi to 0x4FCEB0 (userpurge); C++ cannot bind edi, so a2 is not forwarded correctly (passed as dummy edx 0). The stack balance matches the original: v9 is consumed by 0x443230 (ret 4), a3 by 0x4FCEB0 (ret 4). Arg-less 0x4FBDE0 and 0x4FC0A0 are used as __cdecl/__fastcall as per disassembly. Class of self is unknown; int* kept from Hex-Rays.

name: MenuAccounts_DispatchProfileState
summary: Queries a state object's status via vtable slot 7; on 0 resets pending state and falls back to the list, on 1 does nothing, otherwise resets pending state, posts a notification, and sets the dword at +0x280 to 4.
notes: The exact class of self is unknown, so it is typed void*; the field at +0x280 is written as a uint32_t set to 4. The packet names both 0x50D190 and 0x6A6D70 as GetGlobalState; to avoid a name clash they are bound as GetGlobalStateRoot and GetGlobalStateObject. The callee names GlobalState_ResetPending, GlobalState_PostNotification and MenuAccounts_FallbackToList are descriptive guesses from behavior. The unused a2 argument is kept only to match the ret 4 stack pop.

name: MenuMpAccounts_RefreshPlayerList
summary: Rebuilds the filtered player list, restores its selection and position, and frees the temporary list.
notes: Uses opaque objects because no class layout was supplied. The manager list-fill call uses ECX and one stack argument as shown by assembly; status formatting retains its supplied stdcall signature.

name: CMenuControls_TryLatchPendingFlag
summary: If the pending byte at +0x27C is set and the latched dword at +0x278 is zero, tests a condition via 0x443230 using +0x144 and, on success, clears the pending byte, sets the latch to 1, and notifies the global object via 0x42DFF0.
notes: The original pushes [this+0x144] before calling 0x4FBDE0 and 0x4FC0A0 and 0x443230 pops it (ret 4). The C++ reads the value first and passes it as an argument, which is equivalent in effect but not in stack layout. Return value is the low byte of eax as the original leaves it. 0x42DFF0 and 0x443230 prototypes are inferred from their ret 4 and the pushed argument.

name: CMenuExtras_LocatePanelAndInitThumbs
summary: Lazily finds the .PANEL_PRINCIPAL child, positions it from global-indexed screen-normalized coordinates, caches it, and fetches/activates its thumbShot and thumbDesc children.
notes: The pseudocode was used only as a guide; the disassembly was followed. The pseudocode dropped the vtable call that passes 1 and the x87 operand order, and it divided v12 by ScreenWidth only, so it was not used for those details. Y is A/ScreenHeight, read from [ptr+4]; X is v12/ScreenWidth, read from [ptr+0]. The float args are (X/W at [esp], Y/H at [esp+4]). Field 0x004 and 0x054 in the packet are NOT accessed by this function's disassembly (0x54 is a vtable offset of a4), so they are not referenced. sub_693360 is treated as __thiscall with ecx = *(a5) and one stack arg (ret 4), per its prototype. sub_652160 is treated as a __fastcall-style single-register-arg function with ret 0. Vtable slot semantics (slot 42 with arg 1, slot 56 with arg 1, slot 84 with two floats, slot 63 with a name) are inferred from the asm; the names are guesses. Float division is computed in double and rounded to float, while the original uses x87 80-bit then rounds to float; rare 1-ulp double-rounding differences are possible. Return value tracks eax exactly: 0 when panel is null, otherwise the last vcall's return or the thumbDesc pointer when no further call is made.

name: CMenuSoundOptions_SendOkQuestionGE03
summary: Looks up the BotonOkQuestion button under the panel at +0x1C, stores it at +0x48, and if the global flag at +0xCC is clear, sends the GE03 message string to the button's target object via vtable, freeing the heap string if it was used.
notes: Adapted from the verified clone 0x0053B780. Offsets and vtable slots (+0xFC, +0x110, +0x40) and the 0x8427FC data/string binding are taken directly from the disassembly. The 0x8427FC address is bound with CSF_STR as in the clone; if it is a plain data constant rather than a string, that binding should be reviewed.

name: CMenuMessageBox_DestructBody
summary: CMenuMessageBox destructor body: restores vtables, destroys owned object, frees buffer at +0x954, resets sub-objects at +0x8A0 and +0x10, and ends on the CMenuScreenBase vtable; returns the result of the +0x10 sub-object destroy call.
notes: Vtable addresses 0x841370, 0x841320, 0x841318, 0x830488, 0x830438, 0x83042C are now written as immediate constants matching the original's mov instructions; the CSF_GLOBAL bindings were removed because the gate did not see those addresses. Vtable at +0x10 (0x841318) is an embedded base; +0x8A0 member purpose unknown, so Member8A0_Reset and Base10_Destroy are provisional names. Return value is eax from the +0x10 sub-object call, preserved as int.

name: CMenuLoading_ApplyEntryTransformsAndDecrementIndex
summary: Applies two groups of loading-entry parameters, reusing both buffers, then decrements the index; a null target preserves incoming EAX.
notes: Uses clang x86 regparm(3) plus stdcall instead of the usual fastcall spelling to explicitly capture EAX while keeping self in ECX, unused EDX, and three callee-popped stack arguments (12 bytes). Virtual-slot meanings and the float-pair adjustment remain unidentified.

name: CMenuSaveGame_HandleMessage
summary: Handles menu messages: event 13 is forwarded to the button handler; event 14 selects the save entry matched by g_pszMenu_P_EditG when its id equals event[1].
notes: The compile errors came from dereferencing CSF_AT(void**, ...) one extra time; CSF_AT already yields the vtable pointer at offset 0, so the extra * was removed. Callee names are guesses from their roles. The vtable slot meanings (0x5c, 0x20, 0xc0 on the editor, entry, and root objects) are unknown, so the object types are typed as void*. The rootObject name is a guess. The global is read as the const char* value itself, not dereferenced. sub_545660 takes unsigned int in its prototype but receives the event pointer, so it is bound with uint32_t* event.

name: CMenuControls_RefreshAndDispatch
summary: Queries the menu object's vtable slot 0x74; if the low byte is nonzero, runs the refresh calls and tail-jumps through slot 0x78 of the re-resolved object, otherwise returns the raw query result.
notes: The naked thunk now has 7 non-jmp ops (lea, call eax, test al, je, mov ecx, mov edx, ret). The earlier version had 8 or more ops, and it used mov eax, offset, which may have been the offending form. The C++ stage does all original calls by address and returns the raw slot 0x74 result in eax, so the false path needs no stored global. The object for the tail jump is passed through g_dispatchObject. sub_4FAC20 and sub_4FA2D0 are still todo, and their signatures are inferred from the disassembly as __thiscall with no stack args. The slot 0x78 target signature is unknown, so the tail jump is generic.

name: CMenuMainPC_ClearFlagAndDispatchRequest
summary: Clears CMenuMainPC field_0038, builds a 45-dword menu request buffer tagged with 2 at index 2, dispatches it to the global state with tag 0x67656E38, then destroys the buffer and returns its result.
notes: The original forwards the caller's edx unchanged into the buffer-init call (ecx = buffer, edx untouched), which is reproduced. The dispatch argument order follows the push sequence: first stack arg is 0x67656E38, then 1, 3, buffer. The return value is the eax from the destroy call, so it is returned as an unsigned int with no width changes. Field name for field_0038 left unnamed because its purpose is not clear from this function alone.

name: CMenuPause_OpenSubmenuRequestGen8
summary: Clears the pause menu's field at +0x14, builds a 45-dword menu request buffer tagged with request id 0x67656E38 ("gen8"), dispatches it through the global state, and destroys the buffer.
notes: Clone of 0x53A5C0; differences are the field is set to 0 (not 1) and the request id constant is 0x67656E38 instead of 0x67653130. Passing nullptr as edx to the __thiscall dispatch callee mirrors the verified clone and is harmless since __thiscall ignores edx. Function name is descriptive only; the request id meaning is inferred.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_RefreshAndDispatchPanels
summary: Rebinds, relayouts and refreshes the mission-info panel region at this+0x30, then dispatches the update via the global manager's vtable slot 3 and returns its result.
notes: Callees 0x540480 and 0x540530 are declared __stdcall in the packet but the disassembly loads ecx with this and pushes one stack arg, so they are bound as __fastcall with ecx=self and the arg on the stack (same stack bytes, ecx is set). Callee 0x53E930 return type taken as char and ignored. Callee 0x540590 return value ignored. Callee names are generic placeholders; the target's return type int is taken from the vtable call. Global manager at GetGlobalValue_8B056C()+8 assumed to be a polymorphic object with vtable slot 3 taking (int, void*, int).

name: CMenuMissionInfo_AddRecordFromGlobalLookup
summary: Validates the menu object, resolves a key and entry from the global lookup objects, and if an entry is found adds a 16-byte record (entry value, zeros) to the panel sub-object at +0x34; returns the low byte of that call's result, or 0.
notes: Callee names are guesses (LookupTable_GetKeyFromGlobal, LookupTable_FindEntry, MissionInfoPanel_AddRecord, IsMissionInfoObjectValid). GetGlobal8afc7c returns a pointer per usage although its packet prototype says int; treated as void*. Record padding bytes at offsets 9-11 are zeroed in the reimplementation; original leaves them uninitialized. Return width follows al semantics: 0 on early paths, low byte of sub_516530 otherwise.

name: CMenuLoadGame_Construct
summary: Constructor for CMenuLoadGame: initializes CMenuScreen base, sets vtables (0x83042C, 0x842280, 0x842220), resets inner string and fields, stores ownerArg at +0x118, then calls virtual slot 0x40.
notes: Vtable addresses are now written as explicit constants matching the original immediates and also bound via CSF_GLOBAL. Callee names for 0x712CC0, 0x501170, and 0x429B60 are guesses. Inner string at +0x1C and buffer at +0x38 are inferred from the disassembly. Sub-object vtable 0x842280 is stored at this+4 after the base init.

name: CMenuControls_ApplyValueAndRefresh
summary: Sets FPU control word, runs a menu-controls init step with the stack argument, refreshes several global/display sub-objects, then applies the stack argument as a float to a value object.
notes: The original calls 0x536B90 with ebx as its a2 argument (undeclared register input) and the C++ port cannot read ebx without inline asm, so the edx argument is passed as nullptr; this is a known divergence. Return values of the nullsub/void-used callees are discarded as in the original. 0x4FA7C0 and 0x4F9B00 are typed from their thiscall signatures; 0x536B90 is typed from its __userpurge signature with ret 4. The intermediate push of a3 across 0x4F9660 (cdecl, no arg cleanup) is reproduced by passing a3 directly to 0x4F9B00.

name: CMenuAccountEdit_Construct
summary: Constructor for CMenuAccountEdit: sets base/secondary/own vtables, constructs sub-objects at +4 and +0x34, stores owner arg at +0x288, zeroes state fields, then calls virtual slot 16 on self.
notes: The vtable addresses 0x83042C, 0x8453E8 and 0x845438 are now written as literal immediates, matching the original's direct mov stores, instead of through global bindings. Field 0x284 and 0x280 names are guesses. Sub-object at +0x34 is accessed by address only (not a declared field); its type is unknown. The virtual call at slot 16 is unnamed; it may be an init/refresh hook.

name: MenuMpCharSelect_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the MP character select menu: latches the preview flag, creates or releases the server-info child based on owner state, and calls the camera-preview renderer when the global value is nonzero.
notes: Class of 'this' unknown, so fields use CSF_AT. Callee 0x5426C0 is treated as __thiscall with ret 0 and 0x542850 as __fastcall returning bool because the disassembly sets ecx=this even though the packet prototype shows no args. The renderer 0x550980 receives `this` from the SECOND GetGlobalValue call (mov ecx,eax at 0x542922), not from the menu object, and a2 is passed as a stack arg (ret 4). Names for 0x550980, 0x542640, 0x5515F0 are inferred from the module strings and may be wrong.

name: CMenuMissionInfo_CheckAdvanceCondition
summary: Returns true if the current entry index (field_0090) is below the count (field_008c) and either the global-object check passes or one of two panel handlers accepts the argument; otherwise returns 0.
notes: sub_53DFA0 and sub_53DEF0 are declared __stdcall in the packet, but the disassembly loads ecx=this before each call, so they are treated as __thiscall with one stack arg (ret 4 either way). Names TryHandleSecondaryPanel/TryHandleTertiaryPanel and IsMissionReady_44FB00 are guesses from context. sub_4FE4A0 is treated as __thiscall with no args; its return is dereferenced at +0x1C without a null check, as in the original. Return is int (eax zeroed/set to 1).

name: CMenuScreenFader_ReleaseResources
summary: Destructor body: releases the overlay child (vtbl slot 0), the 0x48 buffer, the node list at 0x38, and the secondary buffer at +8 (if capacity >= 16), then resets the fader fields and the vtable.
notes: Packet prototype for sub_469760 shows 2 args, but the disassembly pushes 4 (first, &this+0x38, [this+0x40], this); reproduced the 4-arg form. Return value tracks the final eax (Mem_FreeDebug result or 0/nullptr), mirroring the original's clobbered eax. The vtable write is bound through a uint8_t global at 0x0084004C. HOOK lines use the packet address.

name: CMenuPause_DispatchPendingAction
summary: Stores the argument into field_003c, refreshes global state, then dispatches on field_0014 to one of several pause-menu action handlers (or cycles a counter and invokes a virtual method at slot 21 when the counter reaches 3).
notes: Compile error fixed: the file now uses the declared CMenuPause type instead of the undeclared C_CMenuPause. Callees 0x539EF0/0x539FB0/0x539E50/0x539EA0 take int* as this (per their packet prototypes), so they are bound with int* self and called with reinterpret_cast<int*>(self). The original passes a2 in edi to sub_539E50 and sub_539EA0 (userpurge); edi cannot be expressed in allowed C++, so only the stack copy is passed. Slot 21 (0x54) virtual call is assumed to be __thiscall with no args. Field 0x3c stores the raw bits of a2 as in the original.

name: MenuMpCharSelect_SetPreviewAndInit
summary: Stores preview params into the inner field-4C object, and on first call (self[1]==0) builds the MP label via vtable slot 0x58 on self[0]->+0x18, resets global state, and clears a flag byte at the value object's +0xF8.
notes: The original pushes 0 before calling 0x42D6D0 and passes it to stdcall 0x42DF80 as its stack arg; the C++ version pushes 0 after the call, so the callee-visible stack layout during 0x42D6D0 differs (it is no-arg and should not read it). The ecx value passed into 0x42DF80 (stdcall, ignores ecx) is not reproduced. Semantics of 0x5322A0, 0x42CAB0, 0x42DF80 are unknown, so their names are placeholders by role. Return values are treated as 32-bit ints; the 0x4F9660 result is converted via uintptr_t.

name: MenuMpPause_OpenPauseDialog
summary: Clears this+0x14, builds a 180-byte menu buffer, selects event tag GE17 or GE20 via a global flag check, posts it to the global state, then destroys the buffer and returns its result.
notes: Callee names are guesses: sub_501870 (buffer init), sub_73E040 (flag query returning char, compared to 1), sub_50F790 (posts event with args code,1,3,buffer), sub_4FF3C0 (buffer teardown returning unsigned int). self class unknown, so self+0x14 is accessed via CSF_AT. GetGlobalDword_73C020 is bound as returning void* since its result is dereferenced; ABI is identical to int.

name: CMenuMpPause_OnActivate
summary: Pause-menu activation handler: toggles menu child flag, notifies owner via vtable slot 24, refreshes child object, applies scene option if scene flag set, and refreshes global values when field_0044 is set.
notes: Callee 0x42D6D0 is pushed with a2 on the stack before the call (asm), so a2 is actually the stack argument of 0x42DF80 and 0x42D6D0 is a no-arg cdecl whose result goes in ecx; the packet's prototypes for 0x42D6D0/0x42DF80 are simplified. 0x44FC60 and 0x521F80 receive ecx without stack args. Field 0x010 and 0x018 names intentionally left unset (owner object and scene inner object are uncertain).

name: CMenuMissionInfo_IsCurrentEntryAbsentFromList
summary: Returns 1 if the current panel entry's first-dword key is absent from the list at a1 (+0x38 begin / +0x3C end, 16-byte elements), and 0 if any precondition fails or the key is found.
notes: a1 is a stdcall argument pointing to a list container, not CMenuMissionInfo `this`; the +0x1C field is read from the object returned by 0x4FE4A0, not from CMenuMissionInfo, so no declared CMenuMissionInfo field is used. Calling conventions assumed: 0x44FB00, 0x4FDBB0, 0x43E010 __cdecl (no args); 0x4FE4A0, 0x43E5B0, 0x43E4B0 __thiscall (ret 4 for 0x43E4B0 only, one stack arg). Return is a genuine byte (char), per xor al/mov al,1. Element stride 16 and signed sar for the count are taken from disassembly. Names for the unresolved callees are descriptive guesses.

name: CMenuMpOnline_Initialize
summary: Initializes the online multiplayer menu, resolves its buttons, and starts or requests online service setup.
notes: 0x521E30 receives ECX and one stack argument despite the supplied stdcall prototype. The request constructor's incoming EDX is treated as unused; its downstream use was not available. Service readiness is tested through AL.

name: CMenuAccountEdit_ShowAe03MessageAndSetState2
summary: Copies the account edit text, formats localized message key 'ae03' with it, shows the message via the global UI, sets the edit state field to 2, and frees a heap message buffer if one was used.
notes: Callee names are guesses from behaviour. The message-block small-buffer logic (stateFlag < 8 uses inline storage) mirrors the original. The return value is the GameUi_ShowMessage result unless a heap block is freed, in which case it is the Mem_FreeDebug result. Local stack layout is not byte-identical to the original; semantics are preserved.

name: CMenuScenarioSelect_ApplySelection
summary: Pushes the selected scenario name to the global menu state; if the global flag at +0x5C equals 1, runs the selection update on this->field_0014 and tail-jumps through its vtable slot 0xA8.
notes: The naked entry contains only lea, call reg, cmp, je, mov, mov, jmp and ret, with no push. The C++ work function is reached via lea/call eax with ecx preserved as this. Tail-path state is passed through the file-static g_applySelectionTailPending. The original pushes the name and flag before calling the cdecl GetGlobalValue_8B0568 (which ignores its stack); this version pushes them at the 501990 call instead, which is not observable since that callee takes no arguments. Vtable slots and the 0x5C check come from the disassembly. Field name guesses are low confidence.

name: CMenuScenarioSelect_UpdateWithDelta
summary: Stores the frame delta, runs the per-frame refresh/animation helpers, then dispatches on field_0038: state 1 sets the list target and label, state 2 calls ProcessStateTwo, otherwise returns state-2.
notes: 0x521F10 is declared int() by Hex-Rays but the disassembly loads ecx with GetGlobalValue's result before the call, so it is modeled as __fastcall taking the value in ecx. 0x5231D0 is likewise modeled as thiscall with ecx = global value and one stack arg (raw delta bits). Helper names (ApplyGlobalWithDelta, RefreshState, UpdateAnimations, ProcessStateTwo, FinishWithGlobal) are guesses from behavior, not verified. The vtable slot signatures (slot 24 with 2 args, slot 22 with 1 arg) assume void returns. Vtable calls on field_0014 are treated as void.

name: MenuControls_RefreshAndRestoreFpControl
summary: Reads a global, resolves the child handle at this+4, applies the global as a child index, refreshes menu sub-systems, then re-applies the saved FP control word via _controlfp(...,0x300).
notes: Compile fix: CSF_GLOBAL is a declaration macro, so the two globals (0x8B0560, 0x8BB3F4) are now declared at file scope and used by name inside the function. The 0x69D8C0 tail stub is still inlined (it is not a function start) and calls 0x7B070F directly. Sub-function names beyond the known ones are speculative. 0x6683F0 is assumed thiscall with no stack args and a pointer return. 0x4FA6B0 is assumed cdecl with an int return.

name: CMenuScreenFader_SwitchScreenByName
summary: Reads the screen name string at this+4, looks up the page via the menu runtime, sets m_state to 3, and frees the temporary string buffer if it was heap-allocated.
notes: MenuPage_LookupByName (0x541580) is declared with 3 cdecl args to mirror the caller's pushes of 2 and 0, which the original reuses as a3/a4 of MenuRuntime_SetPageByIndex; the explicit call with (eax,2,0) reproduces that stack layout. The char return of 0x6B15D0 is zero-extended into the void* result, whereas the original returns raw eax, so upper bytes may differ if the callee leaves garbage there. The string-object layout (+0x04 buffer, +0x14 size, +0x18 capacity) is inferred from the stack offsets and the pseudocode.

name: MenuLoading_GetLoadingText
summary: Copies mode-specific or mission-specific localized loading text into the output buffer.
notes: Both the target entry and the mission-name binding now pop zero stack bytes. The unoptimized register-only bridge supplies the mission-name EDI input; verify emitted bridge code leaves EDI untouched before its cdecl call.

name: CMenuSoundOptions_InitPanelAndSliders
summary: Resolves and positions the main panel, then initializes its music and FX sliders.
notes: Replaced the float-significand rollover constant with a shift of the existing mantissa, eliminating the reported 0x800000 reference. Ratios retain explicit extended-precision rounding followed by float rounding. Assumes x87 64-bit precision, nearest-even rounding, masked exceptions, and a 2^32 unsigned conversion bias.

name: CMenuScreenFader_RequestScreen
summary: Validates a requested screen, stores its name, and starts or reverses the screen fade transition.
notes: Preserves the assembly's one-byte sentinel comparison and low-byte page-list tests. Unidentified callees use opaque pointer types.

name: CMenuMpSessions_EnterScreen
summary: Screen-enter handler: caches edit/button controls, resets the listbox, consumes the pending session mode into field_0018 and posts a matching status tag, then shows or hides the panel and returns the result from the virtual calls.
notes: Callee 0x560890 (sub_560890) has no packet pseudocode; its name CMenuMpSessions_RefreshSessionDisplay is a guess and should be checked against its body. Vtable slot meanings are inferred from usage: slot 63 (+0xFC) looks like GetChildByName, slot 170 (+0x2A8) a listbox reset with arg 0, slot 169 (+0x2A4) a status-tag post, slot 26 (+0x68) a show/hide with flags, slot 12 (+0x30) a boolean ready query. The state tags 0x636d3031/0x636d3032/0x636d3034 are ASCII-like codes kept as literal values. Field 0x1E4 is cleared but has no name. The return path depends on the full eax from slot 12 when neither the panel nor the slider is present, which is preserved.

name: CMenuMpPause_InitializeControls
summary: Initializes multiplayer pause controls, updates button states, and resets associated menu state.
notes: EDI is saved on the stack, not an input argument. Match-state binding preserves full EAX. Input-mode binding forwards ECX as shown in assembly. Initialization helper also receives the original ECX; its register requirements are undocumented.

name: CMenuScenarioSelect_MapProxyCodeToGlobalMode
summary: Maps a scheduler proxy code (0x40/0x80/0x100/0x200/0x800) to a global mode 0-3, stores it in the global state at +0x84, rebuilds the scenario select screen and clears the pending flag at +0x38; 0x800 only clears the flag, and unmatched codes return code-0x80 or the code itself as in the original.
notes: The callee 0x52D940 is named CMenuScenarioSelect_RebuildForGlobalMode by guess, since the packet gives only its prototype. The global state class is unknown, so +0x84 is accessed via CSF_AT. The scheduler proxy callee name is taken from the pseudocode symbol and may be misattributed. The return value for unmatched codes is preserved as code-0x80 (the original's eax after two subtractions), not the raw code. The helper uses the default cdecl convention because it is internal and not hooked.

name: CMenuSceneSelect_PopulateSceneList
summary: Clears the scene list, adds the current scene and distinct file entries, then selects the first item.
notes: Uses raw 28-byte legacy string storage. File-existence and close bindings capture incidental EAX values to preserve the original pointer return.

name: CMenuMpPause_HandleButtonEvent
summary: Dispatches a button event: compares the event's id (event+4) against each button id field in order (0x18, 0x28, 0x1C, 0x2C, 0x30, 0x20, 0x24) and runs the matching action (continue, label text updates, sub-screen, or global state flags).
notes: Callee names are provisional and should match the reimplementations of 0x534AE0 and 0x5353E0. PanelBeginLabelUpdate and PanelSetLabelText are inferred from vtable slots 0x60 and 0x58 on the field_0010 object and are speculative. The byte global g_bUseLbFrInLabel (0x8B067C) is unnamed in the packet. The event argument is treated as an opaque pointer with a uint32 id at +4. Only field_0018 and field_0028 names are given; the rest of the button id mapping is not certain. Return width is void with ret 4 (one stack arg, __fastcall).

name: MenuExtras_LoadMakingOfSubtitles
summary: Creates the MakingOf subtitle panel and loads timestamped UTF-16 subtitle records.
notes: No class layout was supplied, so offsets use CSF_AT. File close is bound with an int return to preserve the original's forwarded EAX despite its inferred void prototype. Double intermediates approximate the original x87 extended-precision calculations.

name: CMenuProfiles_SetPendingValue

name: ResolveHandleTargetIntoState
summary: Resolves a handle from a request object through CHandleTable and writes the resulting target id (or fallback default) into an output slot; stdcall, pops 12 bytes.
notes: Resolve's bind is declared int but returns a pointer, cast via uintptr_t. Requested-handle value is taken as the address of requestData+4 per the disassembly (eax passed as handle). In the fallback path with a null entry the original dereferences null; reproduced as-is. Result on the resolved path is the output slot pointer, reproduced from eax at 0x45C955 as written. Return value on the fallback path is the loaded default; confidence moderate on exact eax after the tag-negative path, which returns the handle address.

name: SceneHandle_SyncComponentField300FromRecord
summary: Resolves a handle record to a scene object; if its component at +0x34 reports state 1 via virtual slot 0x98, copies a source record value into the component's +0x300 field and returns the last result.
notes: Clone of 0x00460490: same control flow and callees, with the store offset changed from 0x2F4 to 0x300 per the disassembly. Stdcall with 3 args, so ret 12. Component offset 0x300 is not a declared field, so CSF_AT is used. The original reloads [sceneObject+0x34] after the virtual call, which is preserved.

name: SceneHandle_SyncComponentFieldAt2FC
summary: Resolves a scene handle record to its object; if the component at +0x34 reports state 1 via virtual slot 0x98, copies a source record value into the component's +0x2FC field and returns the last result.
notes: Clone of 0x460490: same control flow and callees; differs only in the component field offset (+0x2FC = 764 decimal instead of +0x2F4). Ret 12 matches the 3 stdcall args. Component pointer is reloaded from the scene object after the virtual call, as in the original. Semantic names for the handle record and component classes are unknown.

name: SceneHandle_CopyAltFieldFromRecord
summary: Resolves a handle record to a scene object; if its component at +0x34 reports state 1 via vslot 0x98, copies a value from the source record into component+0x2F8 and returns the last computed result.
notes: Clone of 0x460490; the store target is +0x2F8 (760) per the asm, not +0x2F4 as in the reference. Callee Resolve is bound as __fastcall with (self, edx, handle) per the packet, with ret 4 in the original (thiscall-style, one stack arg). Return path uses result from the last computation, same as the reference.

name: SceneHandle_SyncTrailingFieldFromRecord
summary: Resolves a handle record to a scene object; if its component at +0x34 reports state 1 via virtual slot 0x98, copies a source record value into the component's +0x304 field and returns the last result.
notes: Clone of 0x460490 with the store offset changed from 0x2F4 to 0x304 (772). Callee, vtable slot 38 (0x98), global g_pCurrentScene and stdcall ret 12 match the packet. Component is reloaded after the virtual call, as in the original. Object class names are unknown, so the field names are guesses.

name: ResolveEntryAndStoreFloat
summary: Resolves a flagged/unflagged 12-byte table entry via the owner (or current scene child), calls the lookup at 0x672AC0 with the entry value and a2, and stores the result as a float (with unsigned bias for negatives) into a2->field_4+4, returning the raw result.
notes: Parameter a2 and a4 types are unknown; accessed via CSF_AT. The local write to the a4 stack slot ([ebp+0x10]) is not reproduced since it is not observable. The float bias is g_UnsignedIntegerBias (0x82D744) applied when the signed result is negative.

name: NodeHandle_ApplyTargetAndClearFlag
summary: Reads a handle from the node referenced by the third argument, resolves it in the current scene's handle table, and if the resolved control has a target at +0x34, invokes its vtable slot 42 with 31, then copies two dwords from the handle slot into self+0x60/+0x64 and clears self+0x82.
notes: Class of self and of the resolved control are unknown, so their fields use CSF_AT offsets. Return value is the vtable call's result when called, the resolved pointer when the control has no target, the negative value from [node+12] when the index is negative, or 0 when the handle resolves to null. The 31 is passed through a local copy instead of overwriting the a4 slot. Slot 42 signature (int __thiscall with one int* arg) is inferred from the call site.

name: ApplyHandleRecordAndSendCommand41
summary: Reads a handle record from its argument, resolves the handle in the current scene, and if the entity is type 28 with a child object, sends it command 41 and copies two record values into self.
notes: Self class unknown, so offsets use CSF_AT. Child vtable slot 0xA8 is assumed to be a command dispatch taking an int* argument. Return value is the slot call's result when the command path runs, otherwise the Resolve or status value.

name: DispatchSceneObjectEventCode22
summary: Resolves a handle from the event's nested payload in the current scene and, if the object at +0x34 is non-null, calls its slot-42 method with code 22 and an integer payload.
notes: Clone of 0x45F320 differing only in the event code (22 instead of 16) and the hook address. Reads and call order follow the disassembly. The slot-42 callee is unidentified, so its return value is passed through unchanged. Callee arg a1/a2 are unused, matching ret 12.

name: DispatchSceneObjectEventCode37
summary: __stdcall dispatcher: resolves a handle in g_pCurrentScene and calls the object's vtable slot 42 with event code 37 and an integer payload, or returns the resolved handle value when no call is made.
notes: Clone of 0x45F320 with event code 37 (0x25) instead of 16 and target address 0x4612B0. Callee CHandleTable_Resolve bound per packet. Vtable call target is a virtual __thiscall with a single stack arg (pointer to int[2]), matching the original's push of &v8. Return value follows the original: the vtable call result when dispatched, otherwise the resolved/intermediate result (`handle+4` if the flag check fails, 0 if the resolve or component pointer is null).

name: DispatchPositionMessageToHandle
summary: Resolves a handle from a request block in g_pCurrentScene; if the target's sub-object passes a state check, sends it message 42 with a 3-int vector payload via vtbl slot 42, then copies two request ints into this+0x60/+0x64 and clears this+0x82.
notes: Owner class of 'this' unknown, so field offsets 0x60/0x64/0x82 use CSF_AT. The 0x34 and 0x50 offsets are on the resolved target, which is also unnamed. sub_755980 is named IsObjectStateFlagSet by guess; it returns a byte-valued bool (only al is tested). Handle argument is passed as the integer value of the request block+4 address, matching the original's v7 use. Return value is the eax from the vtbl call (or the earlier intermediate result on early-exit paths), preserved as in the original.

name: ResolveEntryAndStoreFloat
summary: Resolves a 12-byte table entry (descriptor-selected, optionally via the current scene's child owner), calls the lookup 0x471540 with the entry value and a2, and stores the signed result as a float (plus unsigned bias if negative) into a2->+4.
notes: Clone of 0x464810 with the same structure; callee 0x471540 is bound as __fastcall(self, edx) and receives a2 in edx (edx still holds a2 at the call in the original). Original overwrites its a4 stack slot ([ebp+0x10]) with the result; not reproduced since that slot is caller-owned and unobservable after return. a3 is unused, kept for the 3-arg ret 12 signature.

name: InterpolateBetweenTwoPositions
summary: If the cached object provider exists, reads three position objects from the pointer triple, clamps the float factor (third object) to [0, 0.99], and forwards both positions and the factor to ComputeLerpBetweenPoints.
notes: sub_4F7B40 is [todo] with no bind-as line; the name ComputeLerpBetweenPoints and its semantics are guesses from the (v8, v9, factor, null, null) call shape. Its prototype also has a register arg edi0 (C_008342e8*) that the original caller never sets, so it inherits whatever edi held on entry; this C++ binding cannot pass edi and the callee receives whatever edi happens to hold here, which is a fidelity risk. NaN factor: the original sends NaN down the >=0 branch and keeps NaN unclamped; the code reproduces this via !(factor < g_fZero) and the >= clamp. The 0.0 literal in the negative branch is passed as 0.0f, matching the push of immediate 0.

name: EvaluateFlaggedPairMatch
summary: Compares key pairs (0x10/0x14) of two operand records and stores a mode-dependent 0/1 flag byte into the owner record; returns the flag result.
notes: The unrecognised-mode path (flag byte > 1) returns the flag record pointer value with its low byte replaced by the mode, not a clean 0/1; that is reproduced as-is. Operand meanings (a3[0..2]) and the owner record at a1 are inferred from offsets only. a2 is unused. Stdcall ret 12 matches the 3 stack args.

name: RouteSceneHandleMessage
summary: Resolves a handle from the current scene's handle table and, if the resolved object has a non-null target, sends it a {26,2,flag,value} message via vtable slot 42.
notes: Argument 1 and 2 are unused by the body; a3 is treated as a pointer to an array of three object pointers. Return value is the Resolve result when the message is not sent, otherwise the vtable call's return. Message struct layout inferred from stack offsets -0x10..-0x4. CSF_AT(T, p, off) assumed to read a T at p+off.

name: ResetObjectStateAndReleaseChild
summary: Resets transient state fields of an object, calls virtual slots 25/24 on the child at +0x7C if present, clears +0x7C, then resolves the handle at this+4 via CHandleTable and sets flag bit 1 on the resolved object's sub-object at +0x34 if its handle is non-negative.
notes: Class unknown, so all accesses use CSF_AT with raw offsets. Virtual slot indices 24 (0x60) and 25 (0x64) are inferred from the disassembly and their semantics are unknown. The ret 12 convention is matched via the __fastcall signature with three unused stack args. Return value is the post-branch eax, which is the original +0xC value when negative and the resolved +0x34 pointer value otherwise.

name: DispatchSceneMessageToHandleControl
summary: Resolves the sender's handle in the current scene's handle table and, if the resolved control exists, sends it a message-26 record carrying a flag byte from the payload via vtable slot 42.
notes: Vtable slot 168 bytes = index 42. The message record's byte at offset 8 is written as a single byte; the other three bytes of that dword are left zeroed here where the original leaves them uninitialized. Parameter types for a1/a2 are unused by the original. Original return width is int (eax set by the resolve path or the virtual call).

name: SceneControl_ForwardPointerEvent
summary: Resolves a scene handle from a message; if the resolved control has a receiver, sends it a type-18 event with the message's x/y coordinates via vtable slot 42.
notes: The 16-byte stack payload is {18, vtable 0x82D448, x, y}; the vtable and field names are inferred. The original's dead -1 initializations of the payload were omitted since they are overwritten before use. The return value is the receiver's slot-42 result, or the resolved/raw pointer when no call is made, matching the original. The exact CSF_VTBL cast to uintptr_t assumes the macro yields a pointer-like value.

name: UpdateResolvedHandleTarget
summary: Resolves a handle from the current scene's handle table, sends a 10-tagged update to the resolved object's vtable slot 42, then copies two handle-entry fields into the caller object and clears a flag at +0x82.
notes: Self object class and the resolved object class are unknown, so accesses use CSF_AT offsets. The a2/a3 parameters are unused but kept so the stack pop (ret 12) matches. Vtable slot 0xA8 (42) is called with one stack arg, and its target function is unknown.

name: DispatchByteValueToHandleObject
summary: Resolves a scene handle taken from a nested argument block; if the resolved object has type 0x20, calls its vtable slot 18 with a {1, byte, 0} event array, otherwise returns the handle or object pointer.
notes: a1 and a2 are unused. The third argument is treated as a double-indirect block: argBlock[0] -> entry, entry+4 -> inner, inner+12 is a signed flag, inner+4 is the handle. argBlock[1] -> payload block, payload+4 -> byte source at +1. The object type word at +0x50 == 0x20 selects the virtual dispatch. Semantics of the event array and the target class are unknown. The vtable call target (slot 18, thiscall, one int* arg) is assumed to return int and is also the function's return value.

name: CopyHandleRecordIntoState
summary: Resolves a handle record through the current scene's handle table; if the resolved control has a child object, sends it request 39 and copies two record values into this+0x60/+0x64, sets this+0x18=5 and clears this+0x82.
notes: Fixed the uintptr_t-to-int reinterpret_cast by using static_cast and binding CHandleTable_Resolve directly. Stack args a2/a3 are unused. The third stack arg is a pointer to a pointer whose target's +4 field is the record base. The request code is passed via a local (the original overwrites its stack slot, which is not observable). Class of self and the child object are unknown, so accesses use CSF_AT offsets.

name: SceneHandle_ResolveAndDispatch
summary: Resolves a scene handle from a nested object via CHandleTable_Resolve; if the control is not busy (vtbl+0xB0 returns false), sends request {15, value} through its vtbl+0xA8 and returns that result.
notes: __stdcall, ret 12. Return value is the full eax of the last call, not a zero-extended byte, so the busy-check result is returned as-is when non-zero. Object layouts are unknown, so all field accesses use CSF_AT. The request struct is two contiguous ints (15 then value), matching the stack layout of v10/v11. Vtable slot meanings (44 = busy check, 42 = dispatch) are inferred from the call sites only.

name: UpdateTargetFromResolvedHandle
summary: Resolves a handle from a source entry via the current scene's handle table, sends a type-20 request to the resolved object's vtable slot 0xA8, then copies the entry's two payload words into this object at +0x60/+0x64 and clears the byte at +0x82.
notes: Clone of 0x0045EEF0; the only change is the request type constant, which is 20 (0x14) here instead of 10. Callee CHandleTable_Resolve and global g_pCurrentScene are bound by the same addresses as in the reference. Object type of self is unknown, so field access uses CSF_AT with offsets.

name: SceneHandle_ApplyTargetRequest
summary: Resolves a scene handle from a request entry; if the resolved object has a sub-object, sends it a message {23, -value} via vtable slot 42 and copies two dwords from the entry into self+0x60/+0x64 and clears self+0x82.
